case_name: State of Punjab and Others v Surinder Kumar and Others
facts: This special leave petition is directed against the order of the High Court dated April 4, 1991, disposing of a writ petition filed by the present two respondents.
Notice was issued to the respondents asking them to get ready for final disposal of the case, and accordingly, they have filed their counter-affidavits followed by further affidavits by the parties

In pursuance of certain instructions issued by the Director, Education Department of the State of Punjab in 1990, each of the respondents was offered a post, as per annexures P-1 and P-2, respectively, of part-time lecturer on the specific condition that he could be relieved at any time without notice, and that the payment would be made at the rate indicated therein on hourly basis.
A written statement was filed refuting the claim in the writ petition and giving the references of similar writ petitions which had been earlier dismissed by this court.
The respondents also detailed relevant facts which clearly distinguish the regularly appointed lecturers from the part.-time appointees, and indicate that the writ petition was fit to be dismissed.
issues: Whether the High Court was entitled to pass any order which it thought fit in the interests of justice
Whether the respondents are entitled to rely upon an order of this court which directs a temporary employee to be regularised in his service without assigning reasons
petitioner_arguments: The respondents argued that they were entitled to be regularised in their posts as lecturers with salary on the regular pay scale

They contended that if this court has issued directions for absorption of temporary or ad hoc Government servants on a permanent basis in several cases, it should be open to the High Courts as well to allow writ petitions in similar terms
respondent_arguments: The respondents' written statement refuted the claim in the writ petition and gave references of similar writ petitions which had been earlier dismissed by this court
They detailed relevant facts which clearly distinguish the regularly appointed lecturers from the part.-time appointees, and indicate that the writ petition was fit to be dismissed
court_reasoning: The court held that a decision is available as a precedent only if it decides a question of law
The respondents are not entitled to rely upon an order of this court which directs a temporary employee to be regularised in his service without assigning reasons
A distinction has to be kept in mind between a court whose judgment is not subject to further appeal and other courts
The Constitution of India has, by article 142, empowered the Supreme Court to make such orders as may be necessary 'for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it'
holding: We set aside the impugned order and allow the appeal but, in the circumstances, without costs
cases_cited: State of Punjab and Others v Surinder Kumar
